destination_record.name: Ladakh
destination_record.tagline: Cross Khardung La, ride a camel across the Hunder dunes and wake beside Pangong Tso on a Himalayan road trip through monasteries and cold desert.
destination_record.places: Leh, Sham Valley, Alchi, Khardung La, Nubra Valley, Diskit, Hunder, Pangong Tso, Thiksey, Hemis, Shey

on.places: Leh, Sham Valley, Nubra Valley and Pangong Tso, with the high passes and most camps and guesthouses open
on.activities: Monastery visits, the Khardung La drive, camel rides at Hunder, sunrise at Pangong Tso, river rafting (usually June to September), trekking and the summer monastery festivals such as Hemis, whose dates follow the Tibetan calendar. Days are bright and pleasant, nights are cold, and May can still bring snow on the high passes.

off.places: Leh and the lower Sham Valley; the high passes, Nubra Valley and Pangong Tso are often closed or very hard to reach
off.activities: Winter in Ladakh is for experienced and well-prepared travellers. Temperatures fall far below freezing, many hotels and camps shut, and roads can close after snow. Speciality winter journeys such as the Chadar trek on the frozen Zanskar river (usually January to February) and snow leopard tracking in Hemis National Park need expert planning.

mid.places: Leh, the monasteries and the Sham Valley, with Nubra Valley and Pangong Tso depending on snow clearance and camp openings
mid.activities: Quieter roads, clear skies, monastery visits and photography, with lower prices. Days are cool and nights are very cold, and some camps open late in spring or close early in autumn, so we confirm availability before you book.

profile.overview:
Ladakh is a high-altitude cold desert in the Himalaya, a land of bare mountains, deep-blue skies, river gorges and whitewashed monasteries. Leh, at around 3,500 metres, is the base for the classic circuit over Khardung La to the sand dunes of Nubra Valley and on to the colour-changing water of Pangong Tso, with centuries-old monasteries such as Thiksey, Hemis and Diskit along the way.

It is one of India's most rewarding road-trip destinations, but the altitude deserves respect. Our itineraries always begin with a rest day in Leh and keep a steady pace, and the travel season runs roughly from May to September. Tell us your dates, group size and budget, and we will build the itinerary around you.

facts.capital: Leh, the administrative headquarters of the Union Territory of Ladakh
facts.climate: Cold, dry high-altitude desert; summer days about 15°C to 30°C with cold nights, and winters far below freezing
facts.flight_time: About 1 hr 30 min from Delhi to Leh by direct flight; from Chennai connect via Delhi or Mumbai. Road routes from Manali and Srinagar are seasonal.

reasons.title: Landscapes like nowhere else
reasons.text: Bare peaks, turquoise lakes, river valleys and cold-desert dunes, often within a single day's drive.

reasons.title: Living Buddhist culture
reasons.text: Thiksey, Hemis and Diskit are working monasteries, with monks, prayer wheels, butter lamps and colourful festivals.

reasons.title: The great Himalayan road trip
reasons.text: Cross high passes such as Khardung La and Chang La on mountain roads that are an adventure in themselves.

reasons.title: Clear skies and sharp light
reasons.text: Dry, thin air gives crisp views by day and some of the best stargazing in India after dark.

reasons.title: Adventure and slow travel together
reasons.text: Add river rafting, short treks or a camel ride to the sightseeing, or simply sit by a lake and watch the colours change.

attractions.title: Leh Palace and Shanti Stupa
attractions.text: A 17th-century royal palace above the old town and a white-domed stupa with sunset views over the Indus valley.

attractions.title: Thiksey Monastery
attractions.text: A hillside complex of many storeys with a large Maitreya Buddha statue, close to Leh.

attractions.title: Hemis Monastery
attractions.text: The largest monastery in Ladakh, in a quiet valley south-east of Leh, known for its summer festival.

attractions.title: Sham Valley
attractions.text: Alchi's ancient murals, the Sangam where the Indus and Zanskar rivers meet, Gurudwara Pathar Sahib and the Magnetic Hill illusion.

attractions.title: Khardung La
attractions.text: A very high mountain pass on the road from Leh to Nubra Valley, with wide Himalayan views and thin air.

attractions.title: Nubra Valley and Hunder dunes
attractions.text: A green valley with a pocket of cold-desert sand dunes, where double-humped Bactrian camels graze.

attractions.title: Diskit Monastery
attractions.text: Nubra's main monastery, with a giant Maitreya Buddha statue looking over the valley.

attractions.title: Pangong Tso
attractions.text: A long, high-altitude lake that shifts from turquoise to deep blue through the day, at around 4,250 metres.

experiences.title: Bactrian camel ride at Hunder
experiences.text: A short ride across the dunes at sunset, on the double-humped camels of the old Silk Route.

experiences.title: Sunrise and sunset at Pangong Tso
experiences.text: Spend a night beside the lake to see the light change from dawn to dusk, weather permitting.

experiences.title: River rafting on the Indus or Zanskar
experiences.text: A guided rafting session in the summer months, with the stretch chosen according to water levels.

experiences.title: Morning prayers at a monastery
experiences.text: Visitors can sometimes sit quietly in the prayer hall while monks chant, which is a memorable start to the day.

experiences.title: Stargazing from the lake or the dunes
experiences.text: On a clear night far from city lights, the Milky Way is easy to see.

experiences.title: Leh market and cafes
experiences.text: Browse shawls, Tibetan handicrafts and dried apricots, then rest in a rooftop cafe with a view of the palace.

food.title: Momos and thukpa
food.text: Steamed dumplings and a hot noodle soup, the comfort food of the mountains.

food.title: Skyu, tingmo and khambir
food.text: A traditional Ladakhi pasta stew, steamed bread and a thick local bread, often served in homestays.

food.title: Butter tea and Ladakhi tea
food.text: Salty butter tea is an acquired taste; sweet masala tea and kahwa are easy to find too.

food.title: Apricots and sea buckthorn
food.text: Dried apricots, apricot jam and sea buckthorn juice are local products worth taking home.

food.title: Vegetarian and Jain meals
food.text: Vegetarian food is widely available in Leh. In remote camps choices are simpler, so tell us in advance and we will arrange the best option on request.

tips.title: Rest on your first day
tips.text: Leh is at around 3,500 metres. Rest, drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol and smoking on day 1, and do not rush the first two days.

tips.title: Dress in layers
tips.text: Days can be warm in the sun and nights are cold. Carry a down jacket, thermals, a cap and gloves, even in summer.

tips.title: Protect against sun and dryness
tips.text: UV is strong at altitude. Use sunscreen, sunglasses and lip balm, and moisturise often.

tips.title: Carry cash and expect patchy signal
tips.text: ATMs are mostly in Leh and can be out of order. Mobile and internet connectivity is limited in Nubra and Pangong, and postpaid connections generally work better than prepaid ones from other states.

tips.title: Be respectful at monasteries
tips.text: Remove shoes where asked, dress modestly, walk clockwise around stupas and prayer wheels, and ask before photographing monks.

tips.title: Follow local rules near the border
tips.text: Photography near military areas is not allowed, and the environment is fragile, so carry a reusable bottle and take rubbish with you.

travel_info.visa: Indian citizens need no visa to visit Ladakh, but every traveller must carry a valid original government photo ID such as Aadhaar, passport or driving licence. Some areas, including Nubra Valley and Pangong Tso, need area permits or registration, and an environment fee and other local charges apply. We arrange permits and confirm the current rules at booking.
travel_info.health: Altitude sickness can affect anyone, whatever their fitness. Symptoms include headache, nausea, breathlessness and poor sleep. Ascend gradually, rest on day 1, drink plenty of water, avoid alcohol and smoking, and tell your guide at once if you feel unwell. Travellers with heart, lung or blood-pressure conditions, pregnant women, and families with young children or senior parents should consult a doctor before booking, and should take any medicines advised by their doctor.
travel_info.money: Carry enough cash for small purchases, tips and personal expenses, as ATMs are mostly in Leh and can run out of cash or be out of order. Cards and digital payments work in larger hotels and shops in Leh, but connectivity is patchy in Nubra and Pangong.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Ladakh?
faqs.a: Six to seven nights is the comfortable minimum for Leh, Nubra Valley and Pangong Tso, with a rest day at the start. A short weekend trip of three nights covers Leh, Sham Valley and monasteries only, without the high passes.

faqs.q: Why is the first day kept free?
faqs.a: Flying into Leh takes you from low altitude to about 3,500 metres in a couple of hours. Resting on day 1 gives your body time to adjust and greatly lowers the risk of altitude sickness, so we never plan sightseeing on arrival.

faqs.q: Do I need permits for Ladakh?
faqs.a: Indian citizens need no visa, but must carry a valid photo ID. Areas such as Nubra Valley and Pangong Tso need permits or registration, and an environment fee and other charges apply. We arrange permits and confirm the current rules at booking.

faqs.q: When is the best time to go?
faqs.a: May to September is the main season, when the passes, camps and guesthouses are open. April and October are possible but colder, and from November to March winter makes most of the circuit unsuitable for ordinary holidays.

faqs.q: Is Ladakh suitable for children and senior parents?
faqs.a: Many families visit, but the altitude needs care. We suggest a doctor's advice before booking, a slower itinerary with extra nights in Leh, and skipping the overnight stay at Pangong Tso if anyone is unwell or very young or elderly.

faqs.q: How do we get to Leh?
faqs.a: Flying to Leh Airport (IXL), usually from Delhi, is the practical choice for most travellers. Road routes from Manali and Srinagar are open only in summer and are long, high-altitude journeys, so we recommend them only for experienced travellers.

group_trips.title: Leh, Nubra Valley and Pangong Tso Group Trip
group_trips.summary: Seven days in Ladakh with a rest day in Leh, Sham Valley, Khardung La, Diskit Monastery, the Hunder dunes and a night beside Pangong Tso, with a trip captain and acclimatisation built in.
group_trips.overview:
This group trip covers Ladakh's best-known sights over six nights: four in Leh, one in Nubra Valley and one beside Pangong Tso. The first two days stay in and around Leh so your body can adjust to the altitude before you cross Khardung La into Nubra Valley.

In Nubra you visit Diskit Monastery and its giant Maitreya Buddha statue and walk on the Hunder sand dunes, home to double-humped Bactrian camels. A long scenic drive then takes you to Pangong Tso, and you return to Leh over Chang La, with a stop at Thiksey Monastery. The last full day takes in Hemis Monastery and Leh Palace.

A trip captain travels with the group, and vegetarian and Jain meal options are available on request. Day 1 is a rest day on purpose, and we ask every guest to keep it that way.
highlights: A rest day in Leh at the start, to acclimatise at around 3,500 metres
Sham Valley: Alchi, the Indus and Zanskar Sangam and the Magnetic Hill
Khardung La and a night in Nubra Valley
Diskit Monastery and the Hunder sand dunes at sunset
A night beside Pangong Tso, with sunrise over the lake, weather permitting
Thiksey and Hemis monasteries and Leh Palace
Trip captain with the group and vegetarian and Jain options on request

itinerary.title: Arrival in Leh | Rest and Acclimatisation
itinerary.description:
Arrive at Leh Airport and meet your trip captain.
Transfer to your hotel and check in.
Rest for the whole day, which is essential at around 3,500 metres.
Drink plenty of water, eat light and avoid alcohol and smoking.
Overnight stay in Leh.

itinerary.title: Sham Valley | Magnetic Hill | Sangam | Alchi
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, drive west from Leh along the Indus valley.
See the Magnetic Hill, where vehicles appear to roll uphill, and visit Gurudwara Pathar Sahib.
Stop at the Sangam, where the Indus and Zanskar rivers meet, and continue to Alchi to see its ancient monastery.
Return to Leh in the afternoon and rest.
Overnight stay in Leh.

itinerary.title: Leh to Nubra Valley via Khardung La | Diskit | Hunder Dunes
itinerary.description:
After an early breakfast, drive north from Leh to Khardung La, at around 5,300 metres.
Stay at the pass only briefly, as the air is very thin.
Continue down into Nubra Valley, a journey of about five to six hours with stops.
Visit Diskit Monastery and its giant Maitreya Buddha statue.
Walk on the Hunder sand dunes at sunset; a Bactrian camel ride is optional and paid locally.
Dinner and overnight stay at a camp or guesthouse in Nubra Valley.

itinerary.title: Nubra Valley to Pangong Tso via Shyok
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, drive from Nubra Valley to Pangong Tso along the Shyok river route, about seven to eight hours with stops.
The road is rough in places and the scenery is remote and dramatic.
Arrive in time to see the lake change colour in the evening light.
Facilities at the lake are basic and nights are very cold.
Dinner and overnight stay at a camp or guesthouse beside Pangong Tso, at around 4,250 metres.

itinerary.title: Pangong Tso to Leh via Chang La | Thiksey Monastery
itinerary.description:
Rise early to see the lake at sunrise, weather permitting.
After breakfast, drive back towards Leh over Chang La, at around 5,300 metres, a journey of about five to six hours.
Visit Thiksey Monastery, with its large Maitreya Buddha statue, time permitting.
Check in at your hotel in Leh and rest.
Overnight stay in Leh.

itinerary.title: Hemis Monastery | Leh Palace | Local Market
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, drive south-east along the Indus valley to Hemis Monastery, the largest in Ladakh.
Explore its courtyards and prayer halls.
Return to Leh and visit Leh Palace above the old town.
Use the free time in the main bazaar for shawls, handicrafts and dried apricots.
Overnight stay in Leh.

itinerary.title: Departure from Leh
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out of the hotel.
Transfer to Leh Airport for your flight home.
Many flights from Leh leave in the morning, so please be ready for an early start.

group_trips.title: Ladakh Weekend Escape: Leh, Sham Valley and Monasteries
group_trips.summary: A four-day introduction to Ladakh with a rest day in Leh, Sham Valley, Thiksey and Hemis monasteries and sunset at Shanti Stupa, kept below the high passes so it suits a long weekend.
group_trips.overview:
This long-weekend trip gives you the gentle side of Ladakh in four days. You fly into Leh and rest on the first day, then explore the Sham Valley with Alchi, the Sangam and the Magnetic Hill, and spend a day among Thiksey and Hemis monasteries, Leh Palace and Shanti Stupa.

The trip does not cross any high pass, so it is a sensible first taste of Ladakh and suits travellers who cannot take a full week. A trip captain travels with the group, and vegetarian and Jain meal options are available on request.

Alchi, the Indus and Zanskar Sangam and the Magnetic Hill in the Sham Valley
Thiksey Monastery and the large Maitreya Buddha statue
Hemis Monastery, the largest in Ladakh
Leh Palace and sunset from Shanti Stupa

honeymoon_trips.title: Ladakh Honeymoon: Leh, Hunder Dunes and a Night at Pangong Tso
honeymoon_trips.summary: Six nights for two across Leh, Nubra Valley and Pangong Tso by private car, with a flower welcome, a candlelight dinner, a couples spa session and an evening by the lake.
honeymoon_trips.overview:
This private honeymoon follows the classic Ladakh circuit at an easy pace: four nights in Leh, one in Nubra Valley and one beside Pangong Tso. You travel by private car with your own driver, start most mornings late, and keep the first day free for rest at altitude.

Highlights include Leh Palace and Shanti Stupa, the drive over Khardung La, Diskit Monastery, a walk on the Hunder dunes at sunset and an evening beside Pangong Tso, when the lake changes colour and, if the sky is clear, the stars come out. Back in Leh you have a couples spa session and time to visit Hemis Monastery.

Expect a flower welcome and room decoration on arrival and a candlelight dinner in Leh, all subject to availability. Please share your wedding date at booking.
highlights: Private car and driver throughout, with unhurried mornings
Rest day at the start to acclimatise in Leh
Leh Palace and sunset at Shanti Stupa
Khardung La, Diskit Monastery and the Hunder dunes at sunset

itinerary.title: Nubra Valley to Pangong Tso via Shyok | Evening by the Lake

After a relaxed breakfast, drive to Pangong Tso along the Shyok river route, about seven to eight hours with stops.
Check in at your camp or guesthouse beside the lake, at around 4,250 metres.

custom_trips.title: Ladakh Classic: Leh, Sham Valley, Nubra Valley and Pangong Tso
custom_trips.summary: A private eight-day Ladakh circuit with two easy days in Leh, Sham Valley, Khardung La, Diskit, the Hunder dunes, a night at Pangong Tso and Hemis Monastery.
custom_trips.overview:
This private classic circuit gives you time at every stage: five nights in Leh, one in Nubra Valley and one beside Pangong Tso. Two days around Leh and the Sham Valley let you acclimatise before the high passes, and a spare half-day in Leh at the end gives you room for Hemis Monastery and the market.

You cross Khardung La into Nubra Valley, visit Diskit Monastery and the Hunder dunes, and drive on to Pangong Tso. You return over Chang La, stopping at Thiksey Monastery on the way into Leh.

The trip is private, with your own vehicle and driver, and you can add days, change hotels or skip Pangong Tso if you prefer.

Alchi, the Sangam, Magnetic Hill and Gurudwara Pathar Sahib in the Sham Valley
Khardung La, Diskit Monastery and the Hunder dunes
